construct: Alpha-intercalated cells in the distal nephron secrete hydrogen ions through apical H+-ATPase and H+/K+-ATPase while returning newly generated bicarbonate to blood. Failure of distal proton secretion prevents adequate urinary acidification, producing a normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with inappropriately alkaline urine, hypocitraturia, and calcium-phosphate nephrolithiasis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Normal-anion-gap acidosis with hypokalemia, persistently alkaline urine despite systemic acidosis, and calcium-phosphate stones localizes to impaired distal H+ secretion by alpha-intercalated cells.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Proximal RTA also causes normal-anion-gap acidosis, but once plasma bicarbonate falls the intact distal nephron can acidify urine; persistent urine pH 6.2 during systemic acidosis argues against it.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The acid-base pattern and nephrolithiasis make defective alpha-intercalated-cell proton secretion the unique transport defect.
